ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a parallelogram, with A at the upper left, B at the upper right, C at the lower right, and D at the lower left. The two diagonals AC and DB intersect at point F. In the figure at point D, 59° is marked between side DA and diagonal DB; at point F, 49° is marked, and it is a pair of vertical angles with ∠AFD. A, F, and C are on the same straight line AC. Reasoning: Because F is on AC, the required ∠DAC is equal to ∠DAF. In triangle ADF, ∠ADF = 59°. Also because the 49° marked at point F and ∠AFD are vertical angles, ∠AFD = 49°. The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, therefore ∠DAF = 180° − 59° − 49° = 72°. So m∠DAC = 72°.

raw_record.question_text: Use parallelogram ABCD to find $m\angle DAC$

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: ABCD is drawn as a parallelogram with diagonals AC and DB intersecting at F. The marked 59° angle is at D between DA and DB, so it is ∠ADF. The marked 49° angle at F is vertical to ∠AFD, so ∠AFD is also 49°. Since A, F, and C are collinear on diagonal AC, the desired ∠DAC equals ∠DAF. Now use triangle ADF: ∠DAF = 180° − 59° − 49° = 72°. Therefore m∠DAC = 72°.
